newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end up on Russia rumor but off highs.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end up on Russia rumor but off highs.

text.p: CME hog futures finished with pared gains as traders became suspicious over a early runup linked to talk of Russian pork purchases, especially when indications on cash markets remained weak, traders said.
Hog futures were due to correct after the recent dip that took October to its lowest level since late March on Monday.

A rumor that Russia was buying six million or more lbs of U.S. pork carcasses and trimmings added to the recovery, but follow through was lacking as the market took time to study the rumor and realized it was actually for a small amount of pork from a normal customer, traders said.

"The Russian rumor is less than a one day's supply, as far as numbers are concerned. They buy from us all the time and they are one of our better customers," said Dave Maher with Securities Corporation of Iowa.

Hog futures closed 0.725 cent per lb higher to unchanged with October up 0.350 at 70.200 cents after climbing to 70.650 cents early. Pork bellies also finished under highs, 1.450 cent higher to 0.500 lower with February up 1.000 at 70.950 cents.
Traders said pressure in the hog pit also developed late in the session on indications cash hog pricess Wednesday would fall further.
Cash pork prices also exhibited a weak tone again Tuesday, sources noted.
